source_excerpts.text:
## 2. A precise additive-expansion target is unattainable

The strongest concrete obstruction is elementary and unconditional.

### Bounded-exponent scalarisation theorem

Let
\[
A\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,B\}^{n},
\]
and let
\[
E_\ell(A)=
\bigcup_{k=1}^{\ell}
\{a_1+\cdots+a_k:a_i\in A\}.
\]

For arbitrary positive integer weights \(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_n\), define
\[
A^\beta=\{\langle\beta,a\rangle:a\in A\}.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
\left|\bigcup_{k=1}^{\ell}kA^\beta\right|
\le |E_\ell(A)|
\le(\ell B+1)^n.
}
\]

This holds **regardless of the magnitude or representation cost of the weights**.

**Proof.** Every vector sum belongs to the integer box
\[
\{0,1,\ldots,\ell B\}^{n}.
\]
The scalar sumset is its image under \(v\mapsto\langle\beta,v\rangle\). Taking an image cannot increase cardinality.

Moreover, the first inequality can be made an equality: choose
\[
\beta_j=(\ell B+1)^{j-1}.
\]
Radix uniqueness makes this scalar map injective on the entire box. ∎

Thus enormous weights can remove collisions between exponent vectors. They cannot create additional exponent vectors.

### Consequence for a recent general-circuit lower-bound proposal

Theorem 2 of Anand Kumar Narayanan’s 2026 preprint *Arithmetic circuit lower bounds from sumset expansion* proposes a sufficient construction with
\[
1\le r\le n,\qquad
m=n\binom{n+r-1}{r},\qquad
s=n^{\omega(1)}.
\]
Its exponent matrix has \(n\) columns and entries bounded by \(2^{n^{O(1)}}\). With iteration parameter \(\ell=s/r\), the required scalar sumset cardinality is at least \(4^s\), after choosing a large weight vector \(\beta\). These are the parameters printed in the version inspected on 11 October 2026. [ECCC](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/138/download)

For any fixed \(c\) such that \(B\le2^{n^c}\), the theorem above gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log_2
\left|\bigcup_{k=1}^{\ell}kA^\beta\right|
&\le n\log_2(\ell B+1)\\
&\le n+n\log_2s+n^{c+1}\\
&=o(s).
\end{aligned}
\]
The last step follows because \(s\) grows faster than every fixed power of \(n\).

Consequently,
\[
\left|\bigcup_{k=1}^{\ell}kA^\beta\right|
\le2^{o(s)}<4^s
\]
for sufficiently large \(n\).

**The expander required by that particular parameter regime cannot exist, even nonconstructively.**

## 3. Changing the iteration count does not rescue the same dimension argument

I then tested whether the obstruction was merely an unfortunate choice of \(\ell\).

For a polynomial map \(f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^m\) with coordinate degrees at most \(D\), define
\[
H_f(\ell)=
\dim_{\mathbb C}
\operatorname{span}
\left\{
f_1^{a_1}\cdots f_m^{a_m}:
\sum_i a_i\le\ell
\right\}.
\]
The constant function is included.

There are two immediate bounds:
\[
H_f(\ell)\le
\min\left\{
\binom{m+\ell}{\ell},
\binom{n+D\ell}{n}
\right\}.
\]

The first counts formal products of the outputs. The second counts the ambient input polynomials in which those products lie.

For a competing degree-\(r\) map
\[
\Gamma:\mathbb C^s\to\mathbb C^m,
\]
the corresponding universal bound is
\[
H_\Gamma(\ell)\le\binom{s+r\ell}{r\ell}.
\]

A sufficient strategy for proving that \(f\)’s image cannot lie in any such \(\Gamma\)’s image would be to make \(H_f(\ell)\) exceed this universal bound. The following result blocks that particular strategy across **all** choices of \(\ell\).

### All-degree comparison theorem

Suppose \(m\le M^r\), where \(M\ge1\), and
\[
s\ge6rM,
\]
\[
s-n\ge
2Mn\left(
1+\log\max\left\{1,\frac{Ds}{rn}\right\}
\right).
\]
Then, for every integer \(\ell\ge1\),
\[
\boxed{
\min\left\{
\binom{m+\ell}{\ell},
\binom{n+D\ell}{n}
\right\}
\le
\binom{s+r\ell}{r\ell}.
}
\]

The proof splits at
\[
L=\frac{s}{rM}.
\]

For \(\ell\le L\), compare
\[
\binom{m+\ell}{\ell}
\le\left(\frac{2eM^r}{\ell}\right)^\ell
\]
with
\[
\binom{s+r\ell}{r\ell}
\ge\left(\frac{s}{r\ell}\right)^{r\ell}.
\]
The hypothesis \(s\ge6rM\) makes the second expression large enough.

For \(\ell\ge L\), set \(t=r\ell/s\). Then
\[
\log\binom{n+D\ell}{n}
\le
n\left[
1+\log\max\left\{1,\frac{Ds}{rn}\right\}
+\log(1+t)
\right],
\]
whereas
\[
\log\binom{s+r\ell}{s}\ge s\log(1+t).
\]
Since \(t\ge1/M\), the second hypothesis completes the comparison.

For
\[
m=n\binom{n+r-1}{r},\qquad r\le n,
\]
one can choose \(M\) polynomial in \(n\). When \(\log D\) is polynomial in \(n\), sufficiently large polynomial \(s\) already satisfies these conditions.

**Scope:** this rules out comparing \(H_f\) against the universal ambient bound in this regime. It does not rule out using the actual structure of competing maps, their polynomial relations, or other invariants. In particular, it does not prove image containment.

source_excerpts.text:
## 4. Nonmonomial features genuinely escape a monomial restriction

The preceding bounds do not justify a broader claim that monomial representations are optimal. I obtained an explicit counterexample to that extrapolation.

Let
\[
a=t+t^4,\qquad
b=t^2+t^6,\qquad
c=t^3+t^5,\qquad
d=t^7,
\]
and define
\[
W=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{1,a,b,c,d\}.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{W^2=\mathbb Q[t]_{\le14},}
\]
where \(W^2\) means the linear span of pairwise products.

Thus five features, multiplied only quadratically, span every polynomial of degree at most fourteen.

### Exact certificate

There are fifteen unordered products of the five displayed generators. Their coefficient matrix in the basis
\[
1,t,\ldots,t^{14}
\]
is a \(15\times15\) integer matrix with determinant
\[
-1.
\]

The full matrix is included in the results file. The research note also gives explicit quadratic reconstruction formulas for every monomial, independently exposing the algebra behind the determinant certificate. For example,
\[
t^8=ab-ac+b^2+bc-cd-ad-c-d.
\]

Consequently, the curve
\[
t\longmapsto(t,t^2,\ldots,t^{14})
\]
is contained in the image of an explicit quadratic polynomial map
\[
\Gamma:\mathbb C^4\to\mathbb C^{14}.
\]

### Five monomial features cannot do this

Suppose a five-dimensional space spanned by monomials had a square containing all fifteen powers \(1,t,\ldots,t^{14}\).

There are only fifteen unordered pair products. Their exponents would therefore have to be distinct and equal exactly
\[
\{0,1,\ldots,14\}.
\]

The generator exponents must lie between \(0\) and \(7\). Producing exponents \(0,14,1,13\) forces the generator set to contain
\[
0,\quad7,\quad1,\quad6.
\]
But then
\[
0+7=1+6
\]
is a collision between distinct unordered pairs, a contradiction.

Six monomial features suffice: the exponent set
\[
\{0,1,2,4,6,7\}
\]
has pairwise sums covering \(0,\ldots,14\).

Therefore the exact minimum feature dimensions in this example are
\[
\boxed{
5\text{ for polynomial features},\qquad
6\text{ for monomial features}.
}
\]

This is a genuine representational distinction. It is **not** a scalable computational speedup. The investigation did not obtain an efficient construction of analogous features for an arbitrary succinct circuit, nor a general zero test operating on them.
